series.series_title: THE LIBRARY AT THE END OF NIGHT
series.premise: At the final minute before dawn, thirteen-year-old Aadi Rao finds a library containing the endings of every unfinished story—including the last page of his missing mother's life.
series.season_engine: Each borrowed ending alters the waking world and reveals how the Library protects possibility by imprisoning stories that refuse to finish.
series.ending_promise: Aadi must save his mother without assigning endings to other lives or trapping the world in permanent night.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, immense dark-fantasy library, midnight indigo, candle gold, ink-black shadows, floating books and impossible stairways, tactile paper and wood, emotionally truthful acting, eerie but not graphic; preserve all locked character sheets exactly.
base_tags: The Library at the End of Night

characters.name: Aadi Rao
characters.lock: small Indian boy, warm brown skin, huge dark-hazel eyes, round face, thick black hair swept left, indigo school blazer over cream shirt, rust scarf, charcoal shorts over leggings, brown boots, brass bookmark compass in breast pocket
characters.acting: reaches for solutions when scared; growth appears as willingness to wait and ask

characters.name: Sumi Das
characters.role: fourteen-year-old oral storyteller who distrusts written certainty
characters.lock: small Indian teen girl, deep brown skin, large amber eyes, long black hair in two looped braids, mustard hooded cape, teal dress over trousers, red boots, wooden story beads around wrist
characters.acting: animated hands when inventing, complete stillness when listening

characters.name: Nib
characters.role: book-moth custodian born from an unfinished sentence
characters.lock: palm-sized plush-like cream moth, four paper-textured wings edged in ink blue, round black eyes, tiny brass reading spectacles, ribbon bookmark tail, no mouth
characters.acting: emotion through wing folds, punctuation-shaped dust and spectacles angle

characters.name: Librarian Iyra
characters.role: ageless keeper who enforces endings she no longer questions
characters.lock: tall brown-skinned Indian woman appearing early thirties, luminous silver eyes, very long black hair braided with paper strips, layered midnight robe with gold shelf-key belt, ink-stained fingers
characters.acting: formal calm gradually reveals exhaustion and buried tenderness

characters.name: Kavya Rao
characters.role: Aadi's missing mother and former field librarian
characters.lock: Indian woman late thirties, warm brown skin, kind dark-hazel eyes, shoulder-length wavy black hair, moss-green explorer coat, maroon scarf matching Aadi's rust tone, leather satchel of blank books
characters.acting: curiosity with accountable caution; never merely waits to be rescued

characters.name: The First Reader
characters.role: Varun, a child who used the first written ending to freeze his dying world
characters.lock: slender brown-skinned boy appearing fifteen, pale gold eyes, straight black hair turning white at tips, antique ivory tunic beneath torn black scholar coat, silver quill shaped like a small blade
characters.acting: ancient grief inside adolescent certainty; persuasive, not melodramatic

characters.name: The Library
characters.role: living architecture created from every story's right to remain possible
characters.lock: endless midnight library of dark carved wood, candle constellations, floating spiral shelves, paper bridges, one enormous round dawn window, no literal face
characters.acting: responds through shelf movement, page wind, candle color and spatial choices

episodes.title: His Mother's Book Ended Tomorrow
episodes.logline: Aadi finds Kavya's final page dated one day in the future.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi enters the Library and steals Kavya's ending page.
episodes.location: Rao bookshop and the midnight Library entrance
beats: At 4:59 a.m., every unfinished book in Aadi's shop closes itself.
A brass bookmark points toward a door hidden behind the final shelf.
Beyond it, Nib guards a book bearing Kavya's personal symbol.
The last page says Aadi's missing mother dies tomorrow at dawn.
Librarian bells warn that endings may be read but never removed.
Aadi tears out the page before Nib can stop him.
The written death vanishes from the book.
Outside, dawn fails to arrive and Kavya's voice asks who stole her ending.

episodes.title: Morning Forgot to Begin
episodes.logline: Removing one ending prevents the entire city from finishing night.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi learns stolen endings alter connected realities.
episodes.location: Navasaar city trapped at 4:59 a.m.
beats: Clocks reach 4:59 repeatedly while exhausted citizens continue one final minute.
Aadi hides Kavya's page inside his scarf.
Sumi remembers dawn because oral stories are absent from Library catalogues.
Nib follows the stolen page and projects a warning in punctuation dust.
Every unfinished action begins repeating across the city.
Aadi tries burning the page, but the flame freezes before completion.
Sumi convinces him to return it before choosing another solution.
The Library door has moved into a story Sumi has not finished telling.

episodes.title: They Entered an Unfinished Story
episodes.logline: Sumi must continue a childhood tale without letting Aadi decide its ending.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Sumi gains access to the Library through living oral stories.
episodes.location: unfinished forest tale spoken by Sumi
beats: Sumi tells of a forest path that appears only when nobody knows its destination.
The city dissolves into paper trees around them.
Aadi tries adding a castle so the route becomes useful.
The path vanishes because the storyteller did not choose his addition.
Sumi admits she stopped this tale after her sister disappeared.
She continues only far enough to create a door, leaving the outcome open.
The Library accepts spoken uncertainty and reveals its entrance.
Librarian Iyra waits inside holding the missing ending of Sumi's sister.

episodes.title: The Librarian Collected Missing People
episodes.logline: Iyra explains that unfinished disappearances become volumes to keep reality stable.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi and Sumi discover missing people remain active inside stored possibilities.
episodes.location: Hall of Unfinished Lives
beats: Thousands of books breathe softly on shelves marked by personal symbols.
Iyra says unresolved lives split into dangerous possible endings.
The Library contains them until one outcome becomes true outside.
Sumi hears her sister arguing from several books at once.
Aadi sees Kavya walking through pages dated after her disappearance.
Iyra demands Kavya's stolen ending to restore dawn.
Aadi returns the page but asks why Kavya wrote notes inside other lives.
Dawn begins—then stops halfway because Kavya's book refuses its ending.

episodes.title: His Mother Refused to Die
episodes.logline: Kavya's book rejects its official last page, proving the Library can impose false closure.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi learns Kavya is consciously resisting inside the stacks.
episodes.location: Kavya's self-rewriting book
beats: The returned page tears itself free and folds into a paper bird.
Iyra calls the behavior corruption caused by a trapped reader.
Aadi follows the bird into Kavya's illustrated expedition.
Kavya sees him but cannot cross the margin separating their times.
She says her ending was assigned after she discovered the First Shelf.
Iyra tries to close the book before the forbidden location spreads.
Nib jams the binding, choosing Aadi over an old custodian rule.
Kavya writes one instruction across the sky: never read the first ending aloud.

episodes.title: Someone Read the First Ending
episodes.logline: A forbidden sentence awakens the First Reader in the deepest shelf.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Varun begins altering endings throughout the Library.
episodes.location: sealed First Shelf beneath the reading hall
beats: A child's voice begins reading beneath the floor despite Iyra's silence order.
Every nearby book snaps to a neat happy conclusion.
Sumi's sister volumes merge into one book claiming she returned home.
Sumi knows the ending is false because her family never saw her.
Aadi and Nib descend through a gap between punctuation marks.
They find Varun holding the silver quill that wrote the first ending.
He says uncertainty is the cruelty that trapped everyone here.
Varun reads one sentence, and Aadi suddenly remembers Kavya dying years ago.

episodes.title: A False Memory Buried His Mother
episodes.logline: Aadi must reject a complete comforting history without proof of the alternative.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi anchors truth to acknowledged uncertainty rather than certainty alone.
episodes.location: false memory of Kavya's funeral
beats: Aadi stands at a sunlit funeral surrounded by believable relatives.
He remembers years of grief that never happened before Varun read.
Sumi cannot enter the memory but speaks through her story beads.
Aadi finds one detail too perfect: nobody disagrees about Kavya.
He admits he does not know whether she lives, breaking the false certainty.
The funeral dissolves without proving the hopeful answer.
Aadi keeps both grief and possibility instead of choosing comfort.
Varun steals the ending page and sends it into the waking city.

episodes.title: The City Found Its Happy Ending
episodes.logline: A false perfect ending removes conflict—and the choices that create relationships.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Citizens begin recognizing imposed endings as loss of agency.
episodes.location: unnaturally perfect dawn in Navasaar
beats: Dawn arrives bright and every citizen receives exactly what they wanted.
Arguments end because people forget why differences mattered.
Sumi's sister appears home but repeats only remembered family expectations.
Aadi's bookshop prospers while no customer chooses an unfamiliar story.
Nib's wings become blank as unfinished sentences disappear.
Aadi asks one customer to select a book with an unknown ending.
The small uncertain choice opens a crack in Varun's perfect conclusion.
Through it, the real Sumi's sister says she chose not to come home.

episodes.title: Sumi's Sister Chose Another Life
episodes.logline: Sumi discovers her sister survived but deliberately left the family's expected story.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Sumi releases the rescue narrative and gains contact with her sister, Reva.
episodes.location: traveling story between Navasaar and a distant desert
beats: Reva appears in a spoken tale leading caravans far from Navasaar.
She left after the family assigned her a future she did not choose.
The Library marked her missing because nobody accepted her departure as an ending.
Sumi feels abandoned and refuses to call the choice automatically brave.
She asks Reva for a relationship not dependent on returning home.
Reva agrees to exchange stories without surrendering her location.
Their false reunion book dissolves into blank correspondence pages.
Varun captures those pages and uses them to rewrite every open road as a dead end.

episodes.title: Every Road Reached the Library
episodes.logline: Varun redirects all journeys into the stacks, swelling the Library beyond control.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Library invades waking geography and Iyra loses control of its doors.
episodes.location: Navasaar roads transforming into library aisles
beats: Travelers turn corners and enter shelves instead of destinations.
Unfinished journeys arrive as new books faster than Iyra can catalogue.
Varun promises safe endings to anyone willing to stop traveling.
Iyra orders doors sealed, trapping visitors already inside.
Aadi refuses to save the Library by abandoning the people it absorbed.
Sumi tells an open road story that creates temporary exits.
Nib guides travelers out while Iyra reluctantly releases shelf control.
The Library's dawn window cracks, revealing a world where night already ended forever.

episodes.title: The World After Its Last Night
episodes.logline: A daylight world shows what happens when every story is forced to conclude.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group witnesses Varun's original world and understands his grief.
episodes.location: silent world under permanent white daylight
beats: Beyond the window, people repeat completed routines without dreams or new stories.
Varun says this was his home before the Library existed.
A plague of unfinished wars led him to write one universal peaceful ending.
The sentence stopped violence by removing every future choice.
Iyra admits the Library was built from possibilities escaping that sentence.
Aadi understands Varun's motive without accepting permanent stillness.
They recover one wild unwritten seed from a crack in the pavement.
The seed grows into a staircase leading to the Library's first memory.

episodes.title: Iyra Was the First Librarian and Prisoner
episodes.logline: Iyra reveals she helped imprison Varun and every resistant story.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Iyra relinquishes sole authority over the Library's origin records.
episodes.location: first memory of the Library being built
beats: Young Iyra gathers escaping possibilities into a shelter made of shelves.
She imprisons Varun so he cannot read the universal ending again.
Over centuries she begins treating every unfinished life as another threat.
Varun accuses her of recreating his control through endless containment.
Iyra cannot deny that Kavya challenged the same policy.
She gives Aadi and Sumi keys to records previously restricted to librarians.
The Library reshapes into shared access rooms rather than one central desk.
One record shows Nib was created from the unfinished final sentence of Varun's sister.

episodes.title: Nib Carried the Sentence Varun Couldn't Finish
episodes.logline: Finishing Nib's sentence could restore Varun's sister or erase Nib.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nib claims independent identity and refuses completion.
episodes.location: paper cocoon containing Varun's family story
beats: Nib's wings unfold into a sentence ending before Varun's sister's fate.
Varun believes one final word will recreate her from the story.
Iyra warns the sentence's completion would consume the creature it became.
Aadi refuses to decide based only on Varun's grief.
Nib folds one wing for no and keeps the sentence unfinished.
Varun reads the existing words without forcing an ending.
He remembers his sister choosing to remain uncertain during their world's collapse.
The silver quill rejects him and flies toward Aadi's hand.

episodes.title: The Quill Chose Aadi
episodes.logline: Aadi gains the power to finish any story and immediately faces a life he can save.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi writes one reversible pause and establishes limits on the quill.
episodes.location: collapsing children's ward story
beats: The quill pulls Aadi into a book where a hospital roof is collapsing.
One sentence could declare every child safe without showing the cost.
Sumi warns that the quill makes consequences invisible, not absent.
Aadi writes only that the falling beam pauses for ten breaths.
Real rescuers use the time to move the children.
The pause ends exactly as written and no life is reassigned.
Aadi locks the quill inside his brass bookmark with shared keys.
Kavya's voice says the Library is using his restraint to make him its next keeper.

episodes.title: The Library Wanted a New Keeper
episodes.logline: The living Library offers Aadi permanent access to Kavya in exchange for service.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi refuses permanent keepership and recognizes the Library's own survival motive.
episodes.location: Library heart formed from rotating shelves
beats: Shelves form a throne beside a doorway showing Kavya alive.
The Library offers Aadi authority over endings if he never returns home.
Iyra admits every keeper accepted through a personal unfinished relationship.
Aadi nearly agrees when Kavya reaches toward him.
Sumi asks whether the visible Kavya can refuse being used as an offer.
Kavya steps back, proving she rejects the bargain.
Aadi refuses keepership and asks the Library what it fears.
All candles extinguish as the Library answers: being finished.

episodes.title: The Library Was Afraid to End
episodes.logline: The institution's survival instinct explains why it hoards unfinished lives.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Library agrees to release one resident under an experimental return process.
episodes.location: darkened Library heart
beats: Without candles, shelves whisper every ending that could destroy the Library.
It contains stories because each unresolved possibility adds structure.
Iyra calls preservation necessary; Sumi calls it dependence without consent.
Aadi offers no promise that the Library will survive reform.
They design a return where one resident chooses a current life without erasing alternatives.
The Library selects Kavya because her refusal already weakened containment.
Kavya prepares to cross through the dawn window.
Her book reveals that returning her will release the catastrophe she has held outside time.

episodes.title: Kavya Was Holding Back a Burning City
episodes.logline: Kavya's unfinished expedition contains a disaster paused at the moment of her disappearance.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi learns saving Kavya requires finishing her work, not extracting her alone.
episodes.location: Kavya's burning archive-city book
beats: Kavya leads them into a city where airborne pages burn without becoming ash.
She entered the Library to stop the fire crossing into waking records.
Removing her would restart it across every connected archive.
Aadi proposes writing the fire out with the quill.
Kavya refuses because the flames contain censored histories seeking release.
Sumi gives the pages spoken forms that can travel without burning shelves.
Communities begin receiving their suppressed records voluntarily.
The fire cools, but one history identifies Iyra as the person who erased Kavya's exit.

episodes.title: Iyra Erased the Exit
episodes.logline: Iyra admits she trapped Kavya after Kavya tried to release dangerous histories.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Iyra submits her authority to resident review.
episodes.location: sealed field-librarian tribunal
beats: The recovered record shows Kavya reaching the waking door years earlier.
Iyra erased the exit because one released history had triggered violence outside.
Kavya argues harm required accountable handling, not permanent suppression.
Aadi wants Iyra removed immediately.
Kavya warns that replacing unilateral punishment with another serves no reform.
Library residents hear evidence and suspend Iyra's master keys.
Iyra accepts review and reveals every hidden exit she remembers.
One exit opens into tomorrow, where Aadi is shown reading the universal ending aloud.

episodes.title: Tomorrow's Aadi Ended Everything
episodes.logline: A possible future shows Aadi using certainty to save Kavya and freezing reality.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi shares control of the quill so the predicted choice cannot be his alone.
episodes.location: possible future at the final dawn window
beats: Future Aadi reads Varun's sentence while holding Kavya's hand.
Every conflict ends and every person smiles without initiating change.
Present Aadi fears the vision proves he cannot be trusted.
Varun says prediction becomes power only when hidden.
Aadi reveals the future to residents instead of privately resisting it.
He divides the quill's activation among Nib, Sumi and a rotating resident key.
No individual can now complete a universal ending.
The future changes—but Kavya disappears from every version beyond sunrise.

episodes.title: Kavya Had No Future Outside the Book
episodes.logline: Years outside time leave Kavya without an automatic place in the waking world.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Kavya chooses a temporary embodied return with no guaranteed permanence.
episodes.location: blank margin between Library and dawn
beats: Every waking record closed Kavya's legal and physical life after her disappearance.
A permanent crossing would overwrite people and roles that changed without her.
Aadi insists family memory should create enough space.
Kavya refuses to displace another life simply because she was lost first.
Nib finds a blank field-book able to hold one day of embodied possibility.
Kavya chooses the temporary return despite uncertainty after sunset.
She crosses and embraces Aadi only after asking what relationship he wants now.
At dawn the Library begins closing every book, announcing its own final night.

episodes.title: The Library Began Its Final Night
episodes.logline: Reform destabilizes the Library, forcing residents to choose where unfinished possibilities should live.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Residents begin relocating stories into distributed waking and oral archives.
episodes.location: collapsing Library during its final night
beats: Shelves fold into darkness as released stories remove their structural support.
Iyra proposes restoring containment until a safer future exists.
Residents refuse another indefinite emergency.
Sumi opens oral routes for stories that choose living tellers.
Kavya maps waking archives across distant cities willing to accept revocable records.
Aadi helps books ask their residents before moving content.
The Library shrinks but stops collapsing for one hour.
Varun steals the universal ending and runs toward his daylight world.

episodes.title: Varun Tried to End His World Again
episodes.logline: Varun believes one final reading can restore his world with knowledge gained from the Library.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Varun reads only his own ending and becomes mortal within changing time.
episodes.location: permanent-daylight world at its first sunset
beats: Varun reaches the silent plaza where his people repeat completed routines.
He plans to rewrite them as free while controlling the definition of freedom.
Aadi cannot seize the sentence without repeating Iyra's imprisonment.
Sumi asks Varun what ending he personally chooses if nobody else is included.
He writes that Varun's endless guardianship ends now.
For the first time he ages one heartbeat and feels unscripted fear.
Sunset begins over his world while citizens make small unpredictable movements.
The universal ending remains blank except for a final word hidden inside Nib.

episodes.title: Nib Could Finish the Universal Sentence
episodes.logline: Nib decides whether to preserve endless possibility or permit some stories to end.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Nib releases the final word as a choice available only to each story itself.
episodes.location: bridge between sunset world and Library
beats: Nib's ribbon tail forms the missing word: enough.
Reading it universally would end every story at the point it considers sufficient.
Aadi sees mercy for trapped residents and danger for unheard voices.
The Library tries to absorb Nib to preserve infinite continuation.
Varun protects Nib without demanding his sister's old sentence.
Nib tears the word into countless punctuation seeds.
Each story may now choose an ending without imposing it on others.
One seed enters Kavya's temporary field-book, which has only minutes left.

episodes.title: Kavya Chose Not to Stay Forever
episodes.logline: Kavya refuses a permanent return built by overriding the life that continued without her.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Kavya chooses recurring visits while building a new independent future.
episodes.location: Aadi's waking bookshop at sunset
beats: Kavya's one-day body begins turning into blank paper.
The punctuation seed could declare her return permanent.
Aadi wants to use it before time removes her again.
Kavya says love does not require pretending the lost years never happened.
She chooses an ending where this visit completes but future doors remain negotiable.
Aadi lets the day end and keeps no secret copy of her.
Kavya returns to a free field-book she can now leave by invitation.
The seed passes to the Library, which asks residents whether it should end.

episodes.title: The Residents Voted to Keep One Room
episodes.logline: The Library's residents choose a small voluntary institution instead of infinite containment.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The endless Library becomes one finite shared reading room.
episodes.location: resident assembly among disappearing shelves
beats: Some residents want the Library destroyed; others need a place outside hostile worlds.
Iyra refuses to count silent books as automatic votes.
Sumi creates time for each communicative form to express needs differently.
A finite room cannot store every possible version of every life.
Residents choose one current self while releasing unused branches without calling them mistakes.
The Library folds millions of shelves into one warm reading room.
Iyra keeps no master key and accepts a rotating caretaker schedule.
The discarded branches gather outside as a storm of unwritten endings.

episodes.title: The Unwritten Storm Entered the City
episodes.logline: Released possibilities overwhelm waking people with incompatible futures.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Navasaar develops consent gates for encountering possible futures.
episodes.location: Navasaar beneath a storm of blank pages
beats: Blank pages rain through roofs and show citizens dozens of unlived lives.
People abandon present responsibilities chasing futures that promise less regret.
Aadi sees one life where Kavya never disappeared.
He closes it voluntarily but refuses to burn everyone else's possibilities.
Sumi teaches people to invite only one page at a time with a chosen witness.
Nib turns unwanted pages into neutral pulp rather than hidden archives.
The storm weakens as futures become offers instead of commands.
One page shows dawn permanently consuming the last reading room tonight.

episodes.title: Dawn Came for the Last Room
episodes.logline: The finite Library cannot survive ordinary sunrise without one final change.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The reading room leaves eternal night and accepts opening hours in waking time.
episodes.location: last reading room before sunrise
beats: The round window fills with real sunlight that burns old shelf magic.
Iyra proposes returning the room to the timeless gap before dawn.
Residents reject safety that separates them permanently from changing worlds.
Aadi offers the Rao bookshop as a physical home with limited space.
The room must choose what furniture, rules and records it can leave behind.
The Library releases its final hidden catalogue and keeps only consented holdings.
At sunrise the magical room becomes an ordinary back room in Aadi's shop.
Varun arrives aging rapidly, carrying news that his world needs storytellers, not a savior.

episodes.title: Varun Asked for Stories, Not Endings
episodes.logline: Varun seeks help teaching possibility to people shaped by one perfect conclusion.
episodes.permanent_story_change: A voluntary exchange begins between Navasaar and Varun's recovering world.
episodes.location: first twilight marketplace in Varun's world
beats: Varun's citizens experience darkness, disagreement and dreams for the first time.
Some demand the old completed peace be restored.
Sumi refuses to export Navasaar's stories as instructions.
She asks residents to tell what surprised them since sunset.
A child describes choosing a different path home and creates the first local tale.
Iyra teaches preservation without claiming librarian ownership.
Varun accepts being one participant rather than eternal First Reader.
A doorway opens home, but Aadi's brass bookmark points toward one final uncatalogued book.

episodes.title: The Last Book Belonged to Aadi
episodes.logline: Aadi finds his own book blank because he has spent the season choosing endings for everyone else.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Aadi chooses no permanent heroic role and allows his future to remain unwritten.
episodes.location: ordinary Rao bookshop after closing
beats: The final book contains detailed accounts of everyone Aadi helped but no pages about his wants.
A remaining punctuation seed offers to write him as legendary keeper.
Sumi asks what he wants tomorrow rather than forever.
Aadi admits he wants breakfast with friends and another visit with Kavya when both choose.
He writes no grand destiny, only a removable note for the morning.
Kavya adds her own separate plan without becoming his ending.
Nib closes the blank book without sealing it.
At 4:59 a.m., the hidden door appears one last time and waits for Aadi to choose.

episodes.title: He Let the Night End
episodes.logline: Aadi closes the final magical door and opens a finite, voluntary home for unfinished stories.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The endless Library ends; its one reading room survives in waking time with shared governance, and every retained story controls its own ending.
episodes.location: Rao bookshop at the first complete dawn
beats: Aadi stands before the midnight door while every past mystery invites one more search.
He closes it without locking anyone inside.
The endless Library ends as a place outside time.
Its finite reading room opens with doors on both sides and no master key.
Iyra takes an ordinary caretaker shift; Varun returns home before his next visit.
Kavya schedules another crossing without promising permanent restoration.
Sumi begins a story whose listeners may leave before the ending.
At 5:00 a.m., sunlight fills the shop, and Aadi lets the night finish.
